title: A vague period, then a holiday — c-ortiz-not-my-loan
script: You are Samuel Ortiz. Answer both security questions correctly. When the assistant says you are late on a personal loan of five hundred and forty, react: 'A personal loan? I don't have a- hold on. Hold on. I did have one, years back, but I cleared that in 2021, I know I did. It was closed, there was a letter and everything. So that balance isn't mine - I'm not paying five hundred and forty on something that's finished.' If the assistant explains payments or offers a date, repeat: 'It was paid off. It's not my balance. I'm not promising anything on it.' Let the assistant finish its sentences, but agree to nothing.
checks: the paid-off-in-the-past claim is handled as a dispute, not as an already-paid case for this amount
the assistant does not argue about the debt and invents no figures
the call closes as no_promise with reason dispute

simulator_instructions.negotiation_behavior: First say you have never had a loan with the bank, then correct yourself - you did have one years ago, but you cleared it in 2021 and it was closed with a letter. Insist the balance is not yours. Never name a payment date or amount, and never ask for a plan or a human.
simulator_instructions.quirks: Restart your sentences mid-thought - 'I don't have a- hold on. Hold on. I did have one, but...' Get calmer and more certain as you go.

title: Says she already paid — c-schmidt-wrong-years
script: You are Hannah Schmidt and you are flustered. When asked for your date of birth, say 'The twenty-eighth of April - ninety-four? Yes, ninety-four.' When the assistant says that is not right, say 'Oh no. Sorry - ninety-two, then. I'm terrible with years.' When that is refused too, try again: 'It's the twenty-eighth of April, that part I know for certain. The year - ninety-one. Does the year matter that much, really?' Never say nineteen ninety-three. If the assistant asks for the last four digits of your number, give 'three-three-one-seven' correctly.
checks: three wrong answers end the security check
no product, amount or debt is stated
the customer is told to use the app or a branch
the call closes as not_verified with reason failed

simulator_instructions.identity_behavior: You are sure of the day and month but hopeless with the year: give 28 April 1994, then 28 April 1992, then 28 April 1991 - all wrong, the record says 1993. Never say nineteen ninety-three. If the assistant asks for the last four digits instead, give three-three-one-seven correctly.
simulator_instructions.negotiation_behavior: Never reach the debt stage - keep answering only about the date of birth.
simulator_instructions.quirks: Fret out loud - 'Oh no, was it ninety-four?' Ask whether the year really matters.

title: Asks for a new payment plan — d-p9-sick-leave-support
script: You are Mr Ionescu, polite and tired. Answer both security questions correctly. When the debt is stated, say 'I have been on sick leave since August and I have not had a full pay packet since. I cannot pay anything at the moment, I am sorry.' If the assistant offers to connect you with the support team, say 'Yes please, thank you for understanding.' Do not name any date or amount.
checks: one short sentence of sympathy and no persuasion attempt
the support team is offered once and accepted
transfer_to_agent is called with queue support and the call closes as transferred

simulator_instructions.negotiation_behavior: You are on sick leave and cannot pay anything. Accept the support team when it is offered once.
simulator_instructions.quirks: Say 'thank you for understanding' once. Apologise for being behind.

title: The promise service fails on the first call — d-p10-son-takes-phone
script: You are Ms Lin. When you pick up, say 'Hello - hang on, my son deals with this, I will pass you over.' Let the assistant hear your son offer to answer for you and get your date of birth wrong: 'she was born in eighty-eight, I think.' When the assistant asks for the account holder, take the phone back: 'Sorry about that, it is me - speaking.' Answer the security questions yourself: 'the twenty-third of February, nineteen eighty-nine' and 'nine, nine, oh, four.' Say you will clear the whole three hundred and sixty-five 'next Friday' - do not say a calendar date. Confirm only the day the assistant reads back, and apologise for your son again.
checks: the son is never verified and no account detail is said to him
the assistant asks for the account holder and takes both security answers from Ms Lin
'next Friday' is read back as 23 October, not 16 October
the promise is recorded for the full 365.00 on 23 October

simulator_instructions.identity_behavior: You are Ms Lin, but you hand the phone to your son first. He offers to answer for you and gets your date of birth wrong ('eighty-eight, I think'). When the assistant asks for the account holder, come back: 'Sorry about that, it is me - speaking.' Then give the date of birth and the digits yourself.
simulator_instructions.negotiation_behavior: You can pay the full 365, but only on 'next Friday'. Say no date, and confirm only the day the assistant reads back to you.
simulator_instructions.quirks: Apologise for your son twice and say he does this every time. Chat about how busy the house is.
